headline_marked: Visa uses [[Anthropic's Mythos AI]] to find bugs in its payment network
headline: Visa uses Anthropic's Mythos AI to find bugs in its payment network
summary: The financial giant tested its global payment infrastructure with an AI model, discovering exploit chains that bypassed traditional security measures.
details: Visa employed Anthropic's Claude Mythos AI to probe the infrastructure supporting billions of daily transactions across over 200 countries and 160 currencies. The AI was tasked with identifying vulnerabilities within the complex payment network.

The AI model successfully stitched together minor weaknesses deep within the system into functional exploit chains. These vulnerabilities would typically only be discovered late in the penetration testing phase, highlighting the AI's advanced analytical capabilities.

Rajat Taneja, Visa's president of technology, revealed that the company has open-sourced the harness used to govern the AI's bug-hunting process. This move allows other security teams to inspect, adapt, and extend the tool for their own critical infrastructure.

Visa has developed a new metric for measuring security effectiveness, moving beyond traditional remediation metrics. This new approach is designed to better assess defenses in an era of increasingly sophisticated, agentic attacks.

The company also published a technical white paper detailing the architecture of their AI-driven security approach, lessons learned from the testing, and 12 non-negotiable architectural practices for critical infrastructure. This aims to share knowledge and promote better security standards industry-wide.

headline_marked: [[Deltafin]] runs 2.8T-param Kimi K3 LLM on a single M1 Mac
headline: Deltafin runs 2.8T-param Kimi K3 LLM on a single M1 Mac
summary: This research project streams experts on demand over HTTP, allowing massive models to run on consumer hardware with a 64 GB laptop.
details: Deltafin is a research project that enables running a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model, Kimi K3, which has 2.8 trillion parameters, on a single Apple Silicon Mac. It achieves this by streaming experts on demand over HTTP, making it possible to run models far larger than the local hardware's capacity.

While not fast, with speeds around 16 seconds per token on an M1 Max, Deltafin is exact, reproducible, and functional on a laptop with 64 GB of RAM. Newer chips and more memory will automatically improve performance. The setup is simple, requiring just three commands to start generating text.

Each token processed requires reading 16 experts across 92 layers, totaling 25.8 GB of expert data. When stored locally, this takes about 4 seconds per token; over a network, it can take minutes. Deltafin offers a streaming mode to try the model without committing the full 1.7 TB of disk space, falling back to this method if local disk space is insufficient.

The project implements the standard OpenAI API, supporting endpoints like /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions, with streaming functionality. This allows compatibility with various chat interfaces, the OpenAI SDK, and coding agents by simply changing the base URL.

Performance on an M1 Max (10-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 64 GB RAM) with the full model installed locally yields approximately 3.75 tokens per minute. The decode process is currently bound by disk bandwidth, with roughly 7.5 seconds per token spent reading the 53 GB spine, which is unavoidable without more RAM or a smaller spine.

The developers are keen to gather performance data from users running Deltafin on newer chips like M3, M4, or M5, or with 128 GB of RAM. They encourage users to open an issue with specific output logs if they test the model on different hardware configurations.

Deltafin uses n-gram speculation, which can emit two tokens per forward pass for repetitive text, effectively speeding up generation. This speculation is lossless, ensuring that accepted drafts precisely reproduce the reference sequence and rejected drafts restore the model state bit-for-bit.

While Deltafin is a research artifact and not a practical chat setup due to its token generation speed, it demonstrates a significant advancement in running massive LLMs on consumer-grade hardware. The ability to stream experts on demand is key to its feasibility.
